newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Another Portuguese general to head U.N. Sahara force.
newsitem.headline: Another Portuguese general to head U.N. Sahara force.

text.p: Maj.-Gen. Jorge Barrosa de Moura of Portugal will take over command of the U.N. force in Western Sahara on Dec. 1, succeeeding countryman Maj.-Gen. Jose Eduardo Garcia Leandro, a U.N. spokesman said on Wednesday.
The operation, called the U.N. Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO), includes 230 military observers as well as some 170 civilian staff and nine police.

The troop contingent was reduced in recent months by about 20 percent because of a continuing deadlock between Morocco and the Polisario Front over who should be allowed to vote in a U.N.-organised referendum to decide whether the former Spanish colony should be incorporated into Morocco or become independent.
The referendum was originally scheduled for January 1992, but has been repeatedly postponed.
Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, in a recent report, recommended another six-month renewal of MINURSO's mandate, until May 31, 1997, despite the stalemate over voter registration.
